'''Branden James Dawson''' (born February 1, 1993) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. A native of [[Gary, Indiana]], he attended [[Lew Wallace High School]] and played college basketball for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]]. In his senior season for Michigan State, he helped his team reach the [[2015 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament#Final Four|Final Four of the NCAA tournament]].

==High school career==

url=http://www.nwitimes.com/conferences/northwestern-conference/lew-wallace-s-branden-dawson-is-a-nationally-ranked-recruit/article_880db6f4-387a-5ddd-849b-e50be2dd0718.html | title=Lew Wallace's Branden Dawson is a nationally ranked recruit | work=The Times of Northwest Indiana | date=November 20, 2009 | access-date=June 17, 2015 | author=Hanlon, Steve}}</ref> He had to sit out most of his freshman season, being academically ineligible.<ref name="nwitimes" /> Dawson was selected for the [[2011 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] following his senior year.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://thehoopdoctors.com/2011/02/2011-mcdonalds-all-american-rosters-announced/ | title=2011 McDonald's All American Rosters Announced | publisher=The Hoop Doctors | date=February 15, 2011 | to his numbers, he helped his Lew Wallace get past [[George Rogers Clark Jr./Sr. High School (Hammond, IN)|Clark]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nwitimes.com/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/depth-charges-lew-wallace-boys-basketball-team-to-repeat-title/article_63b9f294-7dc0-5be6-ae64-4ba962f59448.html | title=Depth charges Lew Wallace boys basketball team to repeat title | work=The Times of Northwest Indiana | date=March 5, 2011 | access-date=July 28, 2015 | author=Trembacki, Paul}}</ref> In the regional finals against Western, Dawson had game-highs in scoring and rebounding with 28 and 15 respectively, but his team lost 69–65.<ref>{{cite web | work=The Times of Northwest Indiana | date=March 12, 2011 | access-date=July 28, 2015 | author=Honeycutt, Paul}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 28.7 points, 18.6 rebounds and 5.6 assists for Lew ==College career==

[[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] and [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] among others, Dawson verbally committed to [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] in August 2010.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.theonlycolors.com/2010/8/4/1606040/welcome-aboard-branden-dawson | title=Welcome Aboard: Branden Dawson | access-date=June 26, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626233436/http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/121911aaa.html | archive-date=June 26, 2015 | url-status=dead Dawson had a double-double in the season opener of his sophomore season, having 15 points and 10 rebounds, against [[2012–13 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|Connecticut]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110912aaa.html | title=Spartans Drop Season Opener To Huskies, 66-62 | publisher=Michigan State University Athletics | date=November 9, 2012 | access-date=August 30, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526140223/http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110912aaa.html | archive-date=May 26, 2015 | url-status=dead }}</ref> In January, Dawson's double-double performance versus [[2012–13 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]], with 14 points and 11 rebounds,  was overshadowed by an alleged physical altercation with Travis Carroll; the [[Big Ten]] after reviewing the incident's footage decided not to discipline Dawson.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/01/09/michigan-states-branden-dawson-denies-that-he-punched-purdues-travis-carroll/ | title=Michigan State's Branden Dawson denies that he punched Purdue's Travis Carroll | publisher=NBC Sports | date=January 9, 2013 | access-date=August 30, 2015 | author=Daniel Martin}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2013/01/michigan_states_branden_dawson_17.html | title=Michigan State's Branden Dawson 'bummed out' by negative reaction from Purdue fans | publisher=mlive.com | date=January 8, 2013 | access-date=August 30, 2015 | author=Leung, Diamond}}</ref> Dawson was involved in a fight with teammate and roommate [[Adreian Payne]], just before an away game at [[2012–13 Penn State Nittany Lions basketball team|Penn State]]; both Dawson and Payne were not allowed to start the game by coach [[Tom Izzo]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/8850723/branden-dawson-adreian-payne-michigan-state-spartans-start-wednesday-night-scuffle | title=Tom Izzo benches two starters | publisher=ESPN | date=January 17, 2013 | access-date=August 30, 2015 | author=Katz, Andy}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/01/16/report-2-michigan-state-players-fight-at-penn-state-inn/1840163/ | title=Punches thrown by Michigan State players in Penn State Inn fight | work=USA Today | date=January 16, 2013 | access-date=August 30, 2015 | author=Rexrode, Joe}}</ref> A few days after the incident with Payne, Dawson had a season-high performance in both scoring and rebounding, with 18 and 13 respectively, to help the Spartans overcome [[2012–13 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] 49–47.<ref name="msubio"/><ref>{{cite web | url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1497138-michigan-state-vs-wisconsin-are-spartans-suddenly-the-big-ten-favorite | title=Michigan State vs. Wisconsin: Are Spartans Suddenly the Big Ten Favorite? | website=Bleacher Report | date=January 22, 2013 | access-date=August 30, 2015 | author=Bielawski, Sean}}</ref> He improved to 8.9 points and 5.9 rebounds per game as a sophomore.<ref name="msubio"/>

In January 2014, Dawson broke his right hand, after slamming it on a table during a film session.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/bigten/2014/01/23/branden-dawson-michigan-state-broken-bone-out-4-5-weeks/4802817/ | title=Michigan State's Branden Dawson out with broken bone in right hand | newspaper=USA TODAY | date=January 24, 2014 | access-date=June 18, 2015 | author=Rexrode, Joe}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2014/01/michigan_states_branden_dawson_45.html | title=Michigan State's Branden Dawson breaks bone in hand, out 4-to-5 weeks | publisher=mlive.com | date=January 23, 2014 | access-date=June 18, 2015 | author=Van Stratt, Gillian}}</ref> He posted averages 11.2 points, 8.3 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 28.3 minutes per game during his junior season.<ref name="msubio"/> Dawson returned from injury on March 1, 2014, after missing 9 games, and eventually would lead Michigan State to a [[2014 Big Ten men's basketball tournament]] championship, being named [[Big Ten tournament Most Outstanding Player]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.mlive.com/spartans/2014/02/michigan_states_branden_dawson_47.html | publisher=www.MLive.com | title=Branden Dawson will return for Michigan State's game vs. Illinois, but Tom Izzo has 'no clue' how much he'll play | author=Gillian Van Stratt | date=February 27, 2014 | access-date=February 15, 2023}}</ref>

As a senior, he was named second-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] and Big Ten All-Defensive Team.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2015/03/michigan_states_branden_dawson_69.html | title=Three Michigan State players named All-Big Ten; Branden Dawson named second-team, all-defensive team | publisher=mlive.com | date=March 9, 2015 | access-date=June 17, 2015 | author=Austin, Kyle}}</ref> In 35 games as a senior, Dawson averaged 11.9 points, 9.1 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game.<ref name="msubio"/>  as well as the [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#Final Four|2015 Final Four]] as a senior, where they lost to Duke. "This is the main reason why I chose Michigan State," Dawson said. "It was to be part of championships and Final Fours. It means a lot what has happened over my four years here. I'm never going to forget Michigan State."<ref>{{cite news|last1=Oren|first1=Paul|title=NBA Draft is next step for Lew Wallace grad Branden Dawson|url=http://www.nwitimes.com/sports/basketball/college/ncaa-tournament/mens-tournament/nba-draft-is-next-step-for-lew-wallace-grad-branden/article_e3b6180b-fcde-5217-a2d1-787bbaa9e0b4.html|access-date=June 18, 2015|work=The Times of Northwest Indiana|date=April 5, 2015}}</ref>

During his four-year career at Michigan State Dawson played in 130 games. starting in 121 of them. He averaged 26.6 minutes a game. He averaged 10.1 points a game, and 6.9 Rebounds a game. Throughout his four-year career, Dawson never made a three-point shot in nine attempts.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2014-2015/histcarr.html#INDIV.FCA | title=2014–15 Individual Career History | publisher=Michigan State Athletics | access-date=June 19, 2015}}</ref> At the time of his graduation, Dawson was Michigan State's all-time leader in blocked shots, with 142.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.lansingstatejournal.com/story/sports/college/msu/mens-basketball/2015/04/09/couch-column-msu-top-fifty-additions/25483137/ | title=Valentine, Trice, Dawson belong in MSU's top 50 | work=Lansing State Journal | date=April 9, 2015 | access-date=June 17, 2015 | author=Couch, Graham}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Los Angeles Clippers (2015–2016)===
On June 25, 2015, Dawson was selected by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] with the 56th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]], only to be traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for cash considerations later that night.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-2015-nba-draft | title=CLIPPERS ACQUIRE RIGHTS TO BRANDEN DAWSON | work=NBA.com | date=June 25, 2015 | access-date=June 27, 2015}}</ref> After posting 12.8 points and 10.3 rebounds in 25.5 minutes per game in the [[2015 NBA Summer League]], he signed a two-year contract with the Clippers on July 15.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/clippersnow/la-sp-cn-clippers-sign-branden-dawson-20150715-story.html | title=Clippers sign second-round draft pick Branden Dawson | work=Los Angeles Times | date=July 15, 2015 | access-date=August 30, 2015 | author=Bolch, Ben}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-sign-branden-dawson|title=CLIPPERS SIGN BRANDEN DAWSON|work=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2015|access-date=July 15, 2015}}</ref> During his rookie season, using the flexible assignment rule, Dawson received multiple assignments to the [[Motor City Cruise|Bakersfield Jam]], [[Grand Rapids Gold|Grand Rapids Drive]] and [[Osceola Magic|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |title=2015-16 NBA Assignments |work=NBA.com |access-date=January 3, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150628235947/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |archive-date=June 28, 2015 }}</ref> On December 28, he made his NBA debut, recording one blocked shot in three minutes of action against the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151228/LACWAS/gameinfo.html|title=Paul, Crawford lead Clippers to 108-91 win over Wizards|date=December 28, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160101123732/http://www.nba.com/games/20151228/LACWAS/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 1, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 2, 2016, in a win 2016}}</ref>

===Erie BayHawks (2016–2017)===
On September 8, 2016, Dawson signed with the [[Orlando Magic]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-six-free-agents-training-camp-nick-johnson-cliff-alexander-damjan-rudez-20160908|title=Orlando Magic Sign Six Players|date=September 8, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 8, 2016}}</ref> but was later waived on October 16 after appearing in two preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-alexander-dawson-murphy|title=Magic Waive Alexander, Dawson, Murphy|work=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2016|access-date=October 16, 2016}}</ref> On October 29, he was acquired by the [[Osceola Magic|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Magic.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://erie.dleague.nba.com/16trainingcamp/|title=Nine Players Added to 2016 Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161031085138/http://erie.dleague.nba.com/16trainingcamp/|archive-date=October 31, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 29, 2017, Dawson was waived by the BayHawks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://erie.dleague.nba.com/news/bayhawks-waive-branden-dawson/|title=BayHawks Waive Branden Dawson|work=NBA.com|date=March 29, 2017|access-date=April 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170402001832/http://erie.dleague.nba.com/news/bayhawks-waive-branden-dawson/|archive-date=April 2, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Hapoel Tel Aviv (2017)===
On March 31, 2017, Dawson signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/news/485443/Branden-Dawson-signs-at-Hapoel-Tel-Aviv|title= Branden Dawson signs at Hapoel Tel Aviv|work=eurobasket.com|date=March 31, 2017|access-date=April 1, 2017}}</ref>  In 8 games played for Hapoel, he averaged 8 points and 4.6 rebounds per game.

===Sun Rockers Shibuya (2017–2018)===
On August 13, 2017, Dawson signed with the [[Sun Rockers Shibuya]] of the Japanese [[B. League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Gary's Branden Dawson: 'We're killing ourselves'|url=https://www.nwitimes.com/sports/columnists/al-hamnik/al-hamnik-gary-s-branden-dawson-we-re-killing-ourselves/article_c8dca9fb-e0a7-5aec-8dba-b5b36563fe99.html|work=NWItimes.com|date=August 13, 2017|access-date=November 29, 2019}}</ref> In 10 games played for the Sun Rockers, he averaged 6.6 points and 2.9 rebounds in 12.2 minutes per game.

===Cañeros del Este (2018)===
On July 15, 2019, Dawson signed with [[Cañeros del Este]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Daniel|last=Mérida|title=TODOS LOS «SNACKS LATINOS» DEL MES DE JULIO|url=https://canchalatina.com/2018/08/02/todos-los-snacks-latinos-del-mes-de-julio/|website=CanchaLatina.com|date=August 2, 2018|access-date=January 27, 2025|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Soles de Mexicali (2018–2019)===
On December 19, 2018, Dawson signed with [[Soles de Mexicali]] of the Mexican [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional]] (LNBP).<ref>{{cite web|title=Branden James Dawson New Addition to the Soles|url=http://www.enfuegohoops.com/branden-james-dawson-new-addition-to-the-soles/|work=EnfuegoHoops.com|date=December 19, 2018|access-date=November 29, 2019}}</ref> On January 9, 2019, Dawson recorded career-highs of 25 points and 18 rebounds, while shooting 10-of-18 from the field, along with seven assists in a 111–90 win over [[Correcaminos UAT Victoria]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Correcaminos 90 at Soles 111|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2019-01-09/Correcaminos-at-Soles/328297|work=RealGM.com|date=January 9, 2019|access-date=November 29, 2019}}</ref> In 21 LNBP games played during the 2018–19 season, he averaged 14.2 points, 7.8 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game.

===Gigantes de Jalisco (2019)===
Dawson finished out the season with the Gigantes de Jalisco of the [[Circuito de Baloncesto de la Costa del Pacífico]] (CIBACOPA).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Branden Dawson (ex Mauricio Baez) signs at Alaska Aces |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Philippines/news/594368/Former-players:-Branden-Dawson-(ex-Mauricio-Baez)-signs-at-Alaska-Aces |access-date=April 30, 2022 |website=August 28, 2019}}</ref>

===Metropolitanos de Mauricio Báez (2019)===
In July 2019, Dawson joined Metropolitanos de Mauricio Báez from the [[Torneo Superior de Baloncesto]].<ref>{{cite web|first=José|last=Encarnación|title=Club MAURICIO BAEZ .. Presume Finalmente Haber Afinado Combinacion de Refuerzos … Anticipa Corona Permanecera En Villa Juana.!!!|url=https://dominicanosaroybalon.com/club-mauricio-baez-presume-finalmente-haber-afinado-combinacion-de-refuerzos-anticipa-corona-permanecera-en-villa-juana/|website=DominicanosAroYBalon.com|date=July 29, 2019|access-date=January 27, 2025|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Return to Cañeros (2019)===
On September 3, 2019, Dawson returned to [[Cañeros del Este]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Regresa Branden Dawson a Tierra de Cañeros para esta temporada 2019, Dawson causó muchas emociones de nuestra fanaticada promediando 13.5 puntos por juego en la serie regular y 16.7 tantos por juego en la Serie Final y 2.3 bloqueos. ¡Welcome Back!|url=https://www.facebook.com/canerosdeleste/photos/regresa-branden-dawson-a-tierra-de-ca%C3%B1eros-para-esta-temporada-2019-dawson-caus%C3%B3/2502796376445241/|work=Cañeros Del Este|date=September 3, 2019|access-date=January 27, 2025|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Bnei Herzliya (2019)===
On November 29, 2019, Dawson signed a two-month contract with [[Bnei Herzliya Basket|Bnei Herzliya]] of the [[Liga Leumit (basketball)|Israeli National League]] as an injury cover for [[Jakim Donaldson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.one.co.il/Article/348438.html|title=בשל פציעת דונלדסון: הרצליה החתימה זר לחודשיים|work=ONE.co.il|date=November 29, 2019|access-date=November 29, 2019|language=he}}</ref> On December 14, 2019, he parted ways with Herzliya after appearing in two games due to an injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.one.co.il/Article/349527.html|title=בא לעזור: נואה דיקרסון חתם בבני הרצליה|work=ONE.co.il|date=December 14, 2019|access-date=December 14, 2019|language=he}}</ref>

On March 3, 2020, Dawson signed with [[Cocodrilos de Caracas]] of the [[Superliga Profesional de Baloncesto]].<ref>{{cite web|title=BRANDEN DAWSON SE SUMA A LA NÓMINA IMPORTADA DE COCODRILOS DE CARACAS|url=https://canchalatina.com/2020/03/10/branden-dawson-se-suma-a-la-nomina-importada-de-cocodrilos-de-caracas/|website=CanchaLatina.com|date=March 3, 2020|access-date=January 27, 2025|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Kaohsiung Jeoutai Technology (2020–2021)===
In November 2020, Dawson signed a contract with [[Jeoutai Technology|Kaohsiung Jeoutai Technology]] of [[Super Basketball League]] in Taiwan.<ref>{{cite news |author1=杜奕君 |title=九太新洋將NBA快艇跳跳人助陣 道森13日清晨抵台 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/1853298 |accessdate=2021-04-26 |work=ETtoday |date=2020-11-13}}</ref>

On February 7, 2021, Kaohsiung Jeoutai Technology waived Dawson.<ref>{{cite news |author1=梁偉銘 |title=布蘭登今離台！九太無預警釋出得分、火鍋王洋將 |url=https://sports.ltn.com.tw/news/breakingnews/3434793 |accessdate=2021-04-26 |work=自由時報 |date=2021-02-07}}</ref>

===Hsinchu JKO Lioneers (2021–2022)===
On February 15, 2021, Dawson signed with [[Hsinchu Toplus Lioneers|Hsinchu JKO Lioneers]] of [[P. League+]] in Taiwan.<ref>{{cite press release |title=布蘭登・大勝加盟新竹街口攻城獅 披22號戰袍征戰PLG下半季 |url=https://www.lioneers.tw/pages/announcement-dawson |publisher=新竹街口攻城獅 |accessdate=2021-04-04 |date=2021-02-15 |archive-date=2021-04-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210417121224/https://www.lioneers.tw/pages/announcement-dawson |url-status=live }}</ref> On February 21, 2021, Dawnson made his P.League+ debut and scored 21 points and 13 rebounds in a game against the league leading [[Taipei Fubon Braves]]. On June 4, 2021, Hsinchu JKO Lioneers announced Dawnson would return to the team the next season.<ref>{{cite news |author1=黃及人 |title=也太早了吧！攻城獅宣布大勝下季正式回歸 |url=https://www.chinatimes.com/realtimenews/20210619002014-260403?chdtv |accessdate=2021-06-19 |work=中國時報 |date=2021-06-19}}</ref>

===TaiwanBeer HeroBears (2022–2023)===
On November 2, 2022, Dawson signed with [[TaiwanBeer HeroBears]] of [[T1 League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=台啤英熊網羅PLG洋將！找來前攻城獅「大勝」助拳 |url=https://sports.ltn.com.tw/news/breakingnews/4109614 |accessdate=November 2, 2022 |work=Liberty Times Net |date=November 2, 2022}}</ref> On April 4, 2023, [[TaiwanBeer HeroBears]] terminated the contract relationship with Dawson.<ref>{{cite news |title=例行賽倒數4場 英熊洋將大勝自請離隊 |url=https://udn.com/news/story/7002/7076529 |accessdate=April 4, 2023 |work=United Daily News |date=April 4, 2023 }}</ref>

===Spartans Distrito Capital (2023)===
On April 22, 2023, Dawson signed with [[Spartans Distrito Capital]] of the [[Superliga Profesional de Baloncesto]].<ref>{{cite web|title=BRANDEN DAWSON ES EL NUEVO IMPORTADO DE SPARTANS DISTRITO CAPITAL|url=https://canchalatina.com/2023/04/22/branden-dawson-es-el-nuevo-importado-de-spartans-distrito-capital/|website=CanchaLatina.com|date=April 22, 2023|access-date=January 27, 2025|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Club Rafael Barias (2023)===
On September 10, 2023, Dawson signed with Club Rafael Barias of the [[Torneo Superior de Baloncesto]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rafael Barias anuncia a Branden Dawson como 2do refuerzo para superior distrital|url=https://hoy.com.do/rafael-barias-anuncia-a-branden-dawson-como-2do-refuerzo-para-superior-distrital/|website=Hoy.com.do|date=September 10, 2023|access-date=January 27, 2025|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Indios de San Francisco de Macorís (2024)===
On July 24, 2024, Dawson signed with [[Indios de San Francisco de Macorís]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Indios anuncian a Branden Dawson como refuerzo|url=https://www.cdndeportes.com.do/deportes/indios-anuncian-a-branden-dawson-como-refuerzo/|website=CDNDeportes.com.do|date=July 24, 2024|access-date=January 27, 2025|language=Spanish}}</ref>

On January 27, 2025, Dawson retired from professional basketball.<ref>{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Cavanaugh|title=Spartan Great Announces Retirement|url=https://www.si.com/college/michiganstate/basketball/spartan-great-announces-retirement-01jjj20sjkqt|website=SI.com|date=January 27, 2025|access-date=January 27, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Dawson was born on February 1, 1993, to Leon Albritton and Cassandra Dawson.<ref name="msubio" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2012/02/michigan_states_branden_dawson_1.html|title=Michigan State's Branden Dawson has matured thanks to family in Gary and East Lansing|publisher=mlive.com|date=February 18, 2012|access-date=June 17, 2015|last=Leung|first=Diamond}}</ref> On March 30, 2010, while a junior at high school, Dawson became a father, to a son named My'Shawn.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2013/02/michigan_states_branden_dawson_27.html|title=Michigan State's Branden Dawson challenged with balancing basketball, fatherhood|publisher=mlive.com|date=February 8, 2013|access-date=June 17, 2015|last=Leung|first=Diamond}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2015/03/01/branden-dawson-michigan-state/24206695/|title=MSU's Dawson finds motivation in role as father|newspaper=Detroit Free Press|date=March 1, 2015|access-date=June 18, 2015|last=Rexrode|first=Joe}}</ref> Dawson received a degree in [[sociology]] from [[Michigan State University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/pistons/index.ssf/2015/05/for_ex-msu_standout_branden_da.html|title=For ex-MSU standout Branden Dawson, NBA Draft Combine invitation was a godsend|publisher=mlive.com|date=May 15, 2015|access-date=June 9, 2015|last=Mayo|first=David}}</ref>
